problem.device: satellite electronics BGA solder joint assembly
problem.failure_mode: solder joint fatigue cracking under thermal cycling
problem.failure: Documented aerospace reliability problem: BGA solder joints in satellite electronics accumulate thermo-mechanical fatigue damage from repeated thermal cycling between sunlight and eclipse (~-150C to +120C per orbit, ~5500 cycles/year in LEO), eventually cracking and producing intermittent or permanent open circuits. The failure is field-documented across aerospace electronics heritage programs and is a dominant driver of avionics derating and redundancy mass. This description is qualitative problem-domain context from the engineering literature; no specific incident statistics are asserted here (the engine's own retrieval must find and custody the evidence).
problem.constraint: Any intervention must survive qualification-level thermal cycling (-150C to +120C), must not add more than a few grams per assembly (launch mass), must not degrade heat dissipation path, and must be retrofittable to existing PCB layouts without redesigning the electronics.

sources.problem_basis: engineering-literature qualitative context; no fabricated incident counts

evidence.title: Reliability issues of lead-free solder joints in electronic devices.
evidence.abstract: Electronic products are evolving towards miniaturization, high integration, and multi-function, which undoubtedly puts forward higher requirements for the reliability of solder joints in electronic packaging. Approximately 70% of failure in electronic devices originates during the packaging process, mostly due to the failure of solder joints. With the improvement of environmental protection awareness, lead-free solder joints have become a hot issue in recent years. This paper reviews the research progress on the reliability of lead-free solder joints and discusses the influence of temperature, vibration, tin whisker and electromigration on the reliability of solder joints. In addition, the measures to improve the reliability of solder joints are analyzed according to the problems of solder joints themselves, which provides a further theoretical basis for the study of the reliability of solder joints of electronic products in service.

mechanism_map.intervention: Implement a compliant underfill material specifically designed for extreme thermal cycling conditions, applied between the BGA package and PCB, with coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) matching between the solder joints and substrate
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Reduced thermo-mechanical stress on BGA solder joints by distributing stress through the underfill material, preventing crack initiation and propagation during thermal cycling
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Qualify the intervention through accelerated thermal cycling testing (-150C to +120C) with 10,000 cycles while monitoring electrical continuity and performing cross-sectional analysis to detect microcracks
